Laura — great questions. Below is a concise post-call blueprint plus next steps. I attached a tiny SDK quickstart bundle and a token architecture diagram for your infra lead.

Summary / recommendation (short):
- Sandbox/dev: short-lived user tokens issued from your identity provider (OIDC) -> exchange for Redwood short-lived JWTs via our token-exchange endpoint. Avoid long-lived secrets for local dev where possible.
- Prod/server-to-server: use a service account + short-lived signed JWT flow (STS) or a token broker in your VPC that mints ephemeral tokens for downstream services. This avoids embedding static API keys in containers.
- Rotation: automated rotation provable in logs. We recommend 30–60 day rotation for service account keys, but surface-sensitive workloads can opt for 7–14 day short-lived tokens with automatic refresh.

SDK quickstart contents (attached):
- Minimal Node and Python examples for obtaining an ephemeral token from our /exchange endpoint
- Example middleware to inject token into requests and to refresh proactively based on expiry (JWT exp claim)
- Sample config for routing fallback: high-priority (regional low-latency) -> cost-priority (multi-region fallback)

Laura / Kimberly — 

Following on Kimberly's email, here's the technical addendum I promised. Key points first, then a one-file Node example reference.

Technical addendum:
- Recommended flow (server-to-server): service account private key (rotated via KMS) -> create JWT assertion -> call Redwood STS exchange endpoint -> get ephemeral access token (expiry 15m-1h). The SDK automatically refreshes when expiry < 60s.
- If you run behind a corporate token broker (HashiCorp Vault, internal STS), configure the broker to mint Redwood-compatible ephemeral tokens using our exchange API. This keeps key material off application instances.
- For embed/rerank: include an application-level signing key to sign datasets for offline reranking only; do not use the same token for model calls unless scope-limited.
- Structured output & tool-calling: annotate tool-callable verbs in prompts and enable conservative output filtering. We'll provide a policy template.

Node example (high level, included in quickstart):
- fetch('/v1/exchange', { assertion }) -> receive { access_token, expires_in } -> SDK.setToken(access_token) -> SDK.generate({...})
